title: Homelessness, substance use and mental health services review
subtitle: County housing plan, a new housing affordability strategy, and closed-session updates on housing and property.
overview: Council held a long special meeting on housing and homelessness. It received the consultants' review and gap analysis of homelessness, substance use and mental health services {{vote:m3}}. The report found fragmented funding, unclear roles between the City and the County of Wellington, and long waitlists. It recommended a human rights-based approach to housing, more advocacy to other levels of government, and outcome evaluation. Receiving the report did not adopt its recommendations. Staff will bring recommendations back on October 17.

Council also heard from the County about its preliminary 2024-2025 budget impacts for housing services, driven by rising shelter use and a growing by-name list. The County said it will hold a health and housing symposium. Council then received the City's Housing Affordability Strategy project initiation report {{vote:m4}}. It sets a timeline for a recommended strategy in fall 2024, with a State of Housing Report due in December.

After a closed session, the Mayor reported that Council received information and gave direction to staff on the housing interview findings. Council received information on a potential property acquisition to support housing supply, and no action was taken on it. These announcements had no separate motion.

decisions.item: Homelessness services review and gap analysis
decisions.detail: Council received the consultants' report on homelessness, substance use and mental health services {{vote:m3}}, which allows staff to prepare recommendations for October 17.
Council received the staff report launching the Housing Affordability Strategy project {{vote:m4}}, with a recommended strategy planned for fall 2024.
Council invoked the procedural by-law to allow the meeting to run until 11:59 p.m. {{vote:m2}}, so the housing items could be completed.

debate: A delegate from a local health centre said it was not consulted after submitting its service inventory or in the data validation. The delegate argued the report should not be relied on without full validation and asked Council to decline it. The delegate also noted that the report had been revised after concerns were raised.

Councillors and staff were wary of declining the report. Staff said not receiving it would stop work ahead of October 17. A councillor asked whether a review with the health centre and the hospital would be enough instead of rejecting the report.

Several councillors questioned whether more advocacy to the province and federal government would produce results. The Mayor said the City had already advocated repeatedly for funding for the integrated police and crisis team. Councillors also asked for advocacy on housing funding, not only mental health.

Delegates from the business community said downtown businesses and the public are affected by the situation. A Chamber delegate said the community needs an integrated health and housing plan before tactical steps. They also said the private sector is willing to help.

Councillors pressed the County on how its funding request would shorten the social housing waitlist, how much the City would need to set aside for new units, and what outcomes the money achieves. County staff said they would provide more data and work with City staff on these questions.
